I mean its just rinse and repeat over and over again. you have to start in a country with a airport and harbor or it wont work. Greenland infected = win. pretty boring after 1 or 2 games

So much content. been playing on multiple platforms for years
but computer is the best :D Greenland sucks though

Plague Inc: Evolved is the kind of strategy game where you start with a tiny little disease and somehow end up staring at a map wondering why Iceland is ruining your entire plan.

The gameplay is simple to understand but surprisingly deep. You create and evolve your pathogen, adapt to different environments, manage mutations, and try to spread around the world before humanity figures out how to stop you.

Every game feels different depending on how you develop your disease. Sometimes everything goes perfectly, and other times one country refuses to get infected for absolutely no reason and destroys your entire strategy.

The progression, different disease types, scenarios, and endless ways to experiment give it a ridiculous amount of replay value.

It's strategic, addictive, and occasionally infuriating in exactly the right way.

**9/10 — spent an hour carefully planning global domination, got stopped by Madagascar.**

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Long-term players praise custom scenarios and expansions, despite tedious achievement RNG.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that achievement hunting relies heavily on luck and specific random events, requiring extensive save-scumming and external guides.

citations.review_text:
Destroying the world, one step, er, disease at a time!

Just got the game recently, and its a lovely little specimen. Different varieties of diseases to send at the world, who wouldn't like that :3

I will say, it *can* get repetitive at times if you're trying to obtain genes to make your life easier on harder difficulties, but i find that it didn't take too long.

Of course, everyone is entitled to their own opinion but i do highly recommend the game ^-^


Achievement Hunters beware however! This will not be a quick and easy game for you to just add some basic quick achievements to your profile totals.

Some of them achievements are heavily based on luck, such asBeta Infection and Ndemic Infection. Both of them require you to play a "Vs." game to completion with someone who already has the achievement, so it's entirely based on luck.

Well then, all things considered, this *is* a good game but short in terms of new experiences, apart from The Cure and Xenolith modes [cough cough, it's a Xenocryst by the way, a crystal, not a rock], since after playing through the diseases and scenarios, you're pretty much experienced everything the game has for you to see. Everything else is for the completionists/achievement hunters dedicated in suffering through save-scumming because of the frustrating RNG to see new lore related pop-up text and/or news bar notices, as those even/situational achievements are very specific. 

It's a great game, amazing soundtrack, but it's better for anyone that's dedicated enough to go through it to just get it when it's on sale. Trust me, the difficulty is all just RNG in the game, but yeah, the sense of achievement after completing a run of almost an hour after reloading your save over and over is there. It is a strategy game after all. And if you're dedicated enough to 100% the game, it's better to just look at the main achievement guide by Solara and Ridimo, and follow walkthroughs from Justaslav_ on YouTube. It'll definitely help you a lot.

Overall, I'm pretty much on the fence about it. Don't even bother with the mobile version. Everything else is so much harder there, and you don't even get the option to load and save games. It's a 6.5/10 for me. I love the game, I'm dedicated to completing it, and enjoy the soundtrack. 
Also, Ndemic, please, give us the option to name our saves so we know exactly what we have on our list, from someone who had 120 something saves and had to manually go through them to know what exactly it was that I had in them and delete the ones that were not needed.

Very fun, goes very deep in a way that you wouldn't really expect from the silly little infection game. You can resurrect Dracula, you can unleash revenge of Osiris (via zombies), you can help Santa spread joy as a brain worm, you can send humanity to the stone age, you can spread Gamergate as a fake news campaign, you can wear the white hat for once and try to cure the world instead of destroy (with the cure DLC), you can terraform the earth into an alien rock (with the new aliens and anti-vaxxers DLC)... I could honestly go on and on, and that's without even touching on the custom scenarios part, where you can play other people's creations. The biggest complaint I have with this game is that a lot of the fun storylines (and associated achievements) are gated behind very random events, so it's a massive pain to 100%. Also, if you do ever try to 100% this game and want to keep your sanity, get ready to make the wiki your second home and get comfortable with abusing the save system.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game includes multiple gameplay modes, official scenarios, and custom scenario creation tools.

citations.review_text: I remember playing this game on mobile a long time ago and I really enjoyed it. Now that I'm playing on Plague Inc: Evolved, the gameplay and visuals are even better. The base game has a ton of content and I like the soundtracks that play on certain diseases. There is a lot of diseases, official/custom scenarios, co-op/versus mode, etc. I have made a custom scenario myself and I enjoyed doing it and there are also many amazing custom scenarios that people have made. I also have the Cure DLC and Aliens & Anti-Vaxxers DLC and I would say that both of them are worth it. The Cure DLC is a twist where you are saving the world instead of infecting it. The Aliens & Anti-Vaxxers DLC brings a new plague called Xenolith, which is an alien crystal. This DLC also adds more official scenarios. It's a no-brainer (pun intended) to get this game when it's on sale. Overall, this game is very worth it (even when it's not on sale) and I think anyone who gets this game will have a fun time playing it. Have a good day to anyone who reads this review!
